cases.requirement: The Adapter conformance target is the exact pinned Harness rc5 baseline; newer/default-branch behavior is not protocol authority.
A safe-runtime ALLOW decision delegates through tools/pre-execute and does not itself originate an approval request.
A safe-runtime DENY decision terminates pre-execute without originating approval and prevents tool-body entry.
ASK without reason projects exactly to Harness {kind: ask}.
ASK with reason projects that exact reason to Harness ask without trimming, coercion, or reinterpretation as authority.
When ASK is the final pre-execute decision, ToolRuntime uses its native serviceAsk path rather than an Adapter-created approval orchestrator.
One reached ToolRuntime ASK invokes ApprovalService.request at most once; safe-runtime does not additionally call Adapter requestApproval for that ASK.
Native approval receives the exact execution agent.
Native approval receives exec.name as toolName and exec.callId as callId without generating or translating call identity.
Native approval receives the ASK reason only when present and receives the execution signal.
allowed-once is the only native approval outcome that permits progress beyond approval.
allowed-once does not bypass monotonic guards; a later M4-041 hard denial still prevents body entry.
With allowed-once and no later denial/cancellation, the tool body may enter exactly through ordinary ToolRuntime dispatch.
rejected maps to pre-dispatch denial and the tool body does not enter.
cancelled does not permit dispatch; a late answer after approval cancellation cannot reopen the cancelled approval.
ApprovalService present with no composed answerer resolves unavailable, records the native audit pair, and prevents body entry.
A throwing or rejected approval answerer is contained by ApprovalService to unavailable and cannot permit body entry.
A non-vocabulary approval answerer return is normalized by ApprovalService to unavailable and cannot permit body entry.
When the approval service is absent, a reached ASK fails closed before dispatch and no approval audit pair is fabricated.
An agent-less ASK fails closed without synthesizing an agent/session/Subject or invoking ApprovalService.
One actual ApprovalService request appends one approval/asked followed by one approval/decided with the same Harness-generated ApprovalRequestId.
The native approval/asked event carries the exact ToolRuntime toolName, callId when present, and reason when present; safe-runtime does not fabricate ApprovalRequestId.
The Adapter's existing normalized approval.decided evidence correlates to the Harness-generated approval id and call id on the native ToolRuntime ASK path.
Approval policy never deterministically rejects before answerer dispatch while still producing the service-owned asked/decided audit pair.
ApprovalService requires an open turn; failure of that precondition cannot cause tool-body dispatch.
Failure to commit required approval audit state rejects the approval request rather than returning an unlogged grant; ToolRuntime does not dispatch the body from that failure.
A pre-execute listener that terminates before safe-runtime can prevent the safe-runtime ASK handler from running; M4-042 does not classify this as approval bypass with dispatch.

Because tools/pre-execute is a waterfall, an outer listener may replace a downstream ASK before the final gate reaches ToolRuntime; M4-042 does not claim every intermediate ASK necessarily reaches approval.
Portable protocol actionRef is not inferred to equal Harness callId/callRef; M4-042 preserves the accepted M4-023 correlation boundary.
The standalone Adapter requestApproval port remains separate and is not invoked as a second step for a ToolRuntime ASK.

M4-042 does not own authoritative tools/result composition, duplicate-subsystem repository audit, audit redaction, Lease consumption, Decision/Receipt construction, or final GuaranteeLevel assignment.
Native ASK routing proves only the supported ToolRuntime approval seam and does not imply every host effect traverses ToolRuntime or complete system-wide tool-enforced coverage.
